entries.summary: Shear, the Scale and Transform Each dialogs, the Free Transform tool, the liquify tools and envelopes, as Illustrator has them
breakingChanges: Documents that hold an envelope are refused by 0.7.0 and earlier editors and APIs, which do not know the field (ADR-0034, proposed). Migration: to open such a document in an earlier version, expand or release its envelopes first.

changes.description: Shear with the Shear tool, beside Scale and Reshape: a drag that starts up or down shears along the vertical axis and one that starts sideways along the horizontal axis, about the pivot, with Shift keeping the original width or height; a click moves the reference point first, and Alt-click moves it and opens the Shear dialog, which takes an angle from -359 to 359 along a horizontal, vertical or angled axis, with Copy. Every object keeps its kind, text and pictures included.
Scale with the Scale dialog, from a double-click on the tool, Alt-click or Object > Transform > Scale: Uniform or Non-Uniform percentages, negative ones reflecting, Scale Strokes & Effects and Copy.

Transform with the Free Transform tool (E): its box moves the selection from inside, scales it from a handle against the opposite one, Shift keeping the proportions and Alt scaling from the centre, and rotates it from outside, Shift by 45 degrees. Holding Ctrl+Alt while a side handle is dragged shears along that side, Ctrl on a corner handle distorts freely and Shift+Alt+Ctrl distorts in perspective. Ctrl works whether it is pressed before the drag or during it. Three buttons in the context bar, as the tool's widget in later Illustrator versions has them, choose Free Transform, where a corner scales, Free Distort, where it moves alone, and Perspective Distort, where it moves with its neighbour, so no key needs to be held. Distorted shapes become paths that pass within half a pixel of the exact map; text, pictures, symbols, dimensions and floor-plan objects are left as they are and named.

Reshape with the liquify tools, in a family of their own: Warp (Shift+R) pushes the outline with the drag; Twirl turns it about the brush, counterclockwise for a positive rate; Pucker pulls it in and Bloat pushes it out; Scallop, Crystallize and Wrinkle add curved, spiked and wrinkled details. They act inside an elliptical brush drawn at the cursor, keep acting while the button is held, reshape only the selection when there is one and every unlocked vector object under the brush when there is none, and add anchors at the spacing of Detail. Alt-drag sizes the brush, Shift+Alt as a circle, and a double-click on the tool opens its options with the ranges of the manual, kept between sessions.

Reshape objects with envelopes, from Object > Envelope Distort: Make With Warp (Alt+Shift+Ctrl+W) with the Warp Options and a live preview, the fifteen styles shown by pictures, the axis, Bend and the horizontal and vertical Distortion; Make With Mesh (Alt+Ctrl+M) with its rows and columns; and Make With Top Object (Alt+Ctrl+C), the topmost selected shape taking the others. The objects stay whole inside one Envelope. Edit Contents (Shift+Ctrl+V) brings them out to be edited with every tool while the envelope keeps drawing them through its mesh, and Edit Envelope takes them back, recentred; Reset With Warp and Reset With Mesh, which can keep the shape, replace the mesh; Envelope Options sets the Fidelity; Release gives back the objects and the envelope's shape, and Expand leaves the distorted paths. The Direct Selection tool drags the points and handles of the mesh, the Mesh tool (U) adds a row and a column through a click on any envelope, taking it without selecting it first, and Delete on a chosen point removes them. The canvas, SVG and PDF draw the same distortion. Text is outlined first (Ctrl+Shift+O).
Transform each selected object about its own reference point with Object > Transform > Transform Each (Alt+Shift+Ctrl+D): scale, move, rotate and reflect, with the nine reference points and Copy.

Zoom as Illustrator does. Ctrl+Space holds the Zoom tool over any tool and Ctrl+Alt+Space holds it in reduce mode: a click zooms in, or out, to the next preset about the point clicked, which comes to the centre, and a drag zooms to the area dragged, without drawing; letting the keys go gives back the tool in use. The Zoom tool itself zooms in with a click, out with Alt, to an area with a drag whose marquee Space moves, and to 100 percent with a double-click, as View > Actual Size (Ctrl+1) does; a double-click on the Hand tool fits the page, and View > Zoom In and Zoom Out step through the same presets. A finger tap and a finger drag with the Zoom tool work the same on a touch screen, and two fingers still zoom the view.
Fill the icon of the Selection tool, as Illustrator draws its black arrow, and keep the Direct Selection tool's icon as an outline, so the two are told apart at a glance.

Drag with the Scale tool as in Illustrator: the point pressed follows the pointer on each axis about the pivot, Shift keeps the proportions on a diagonal drag and scales one axis on a drag along it, and a click sets the reference point.
Repeat a scale or a shear with Transform Again (Ctrl+D) as the same map about the same point.
Gather the transformations of the selection in an Object > Transform section of the menu.
Show the Gradient tool in the column of tools, with the Mesh tool beside it, and the liquify and Free Transform tools after Scale; the Gradient tool of 0.7.0 was only reachable with G.

Plan the block in PLAN-0008-0008 with its divergences from Illustrator, and record its scenarios, SC-0109 to SC-0112, and the envelope field of the native format as a proposed decision, ADR-0034, awaiting owner review.

Record the owner's decisions on 0.7.0: ADR-0033, the gradients, patterns and swatches of the native format, is accepted, and the colour tools and the phone layout are accepted visually for the maturity of this preview. The strict Sonar gate remains outstanding, so no scenario is marked Verified.

Keep the affine map of layers, the quadrilateral map, the liquify tools and the envelope mesh of Coons patches in the domain package, tested against geometric oracles; the API validates envelopes as the editor does, and its request schema stops at the layers an envelope holds instead of expanding them forever.

entries.summary: Gradients, patterns, swatches and colour modes, lock and hide as in Illustrator, and a studio that works on a phone
breakingChanges: Documents that carry a gradient or pattern fill, patterns or swatches are refused by 0.6.0 and earlier editors and APIs, which do not know those fields (ADR-0033, proposed). Migration: to open such a document in an earlier version, set the fills back to plain colours and remove its patterns and swatches.

changes.description: Lock and hide objects as Illustrator does: Lock and Hide the selection with Ctrl+2 and Ctrl+3, the artwork above it that overlaps it, or everything outside its top-level groups with Ctrl+Alt+Shift+2 and Ctrl+Alt+Shift+3; Unlock All with Ctrl+Alt+2 and Show All with Ctrl+Alt+3 bring every object back and select it. Keys with a digit are read by their place on the keyboard, so they work on layouts whose Ctrl+Alt types a character of its own.

Use the studio on a phone. The column of tools and the panels become drawers that slide in from the left and right edges, opened with a swipe from the edge or a tap on its handle and closed with a swipe back or a tap outside; the menus fold behind a menu button, with the credits of the footer fixed at their foot; and the page fits the screen, with the drawers scrolling only down.

Switch documents on a phone from a list in the header, between the application icon and the language, which also makes a new document and closes the one shown; the strip of tabs gives its height to the canvas. The document is renamed in Properties, where its name now sits with the rest of the page.

Paint shapes and text with gradients and patterns, stored in the native format with the patterns and swatches of the document and checked on open by the editor and the API. A linear gradient crosses the object along its angle and a radial one spreads from its centre, each with its colour stops and midpoints, and turns with the object; a pattern tiles its artwork from the document origin, as Illustrator lays patterns out. Both are drawn on the canvas and written to SVG and PDF: a gradient as a PDF shading clipped to its shape and a pattern as a tiling pattern, with transparent gradient stops and transparency inside a pattern tile reported as not carried.

Choose the fill in the paint popover as a colour, a gradient, a pattern or none. The gradient editor sets the type, the angle and each stop with its location and midpoint, adds a stop in the widest gap, removes one and reverses the gradient; the pattern picker lists the patterns of the document and five ready-made ones. A gradient or pattern chosen with nothing selected fills the objects drawn next.
Drag the Gradient tool (G) across the selection to set where its gradient starts and ends, across every selected object at once and in one undo step; Shift keeps the line to 45 degrees.

Blend gradients between objects: the steps mix the two gradients stop by stop and turn between their angles or lines, and a gradient blended with a flat colour fades into that colour at both of its ends, step by step, or out to transparent when the other end has no fill. Patterns are not mixed; each step keeps the pattern of the nearer end.
Define a pattern from the selected vector artwork with Edit > Define Pattern; it joins the swatches of the document.

Pick colours in the model you work in: Quick RGB, the default and the picker of earlier versions, RGB sliders, CMYK sliders, a grey level or a custom palette of your own. The model only changes how a colour is chosen; the document keeps it as before. CMYK uses the device formula, without colour management, so it is not a print separation.

Show the Swatches panel from View > Layout, hidden by default: it lists the swatches of the document, starting from a default set, applies one to the fill or the stroke, filters them by kind, keeps the current fill as a new swatch and deletes the one chosen. Gradients and patterns fill objects only, since a stroke takes a colour.
Open context menus with a long press, since a phone has no right button; the canvas, the layers and the guides each open their own.
Zoom and pan the canvas with two fingers, and scale the selection in proportion, turn it and move it with two fingers that land on it, around its pivot and as one step.

Show the properties of the document in Properties when nothing is selected, as Illustrator does: width and height in the ruler unit, the orientation, the ruler unit, the margin guides with their centre guides, the registration marks and the background, each applied at once while the rest of the page setup is kept, with the full Document dimensions dialog a button away.

Select a filled open curve by clicking inside its fill, as a closed one is, since the fill paints it as if closed; an open curve without a fill is still selected by its outline only, and locked or hidden curves never are.

Redraw the icons of the Bezier tools: the Pen as a fountain-pen nib, Add Anchor Point, Delete Anchor Point and Convert Anchor Point as the same nib with a plus, a minus or a small square at its top left corner. The Paintbrush and the raster brush now show a brush with a pointed tip, above a vector path or a painted stroke.
Make the strip of document tabs 38 pixels high and each tab 36, so the tabs sit inside the strip.

Bring the agent instructions in line with the project as it is: the promotion from dev to release and main without qa and demo branches, the docs branches, the licence, the imitation of Illustrator's behaviour and keys, and the preview publishing rules.

Bring the contribution guide in line with the licence and the way the project works now: outside contributions need the author's written agreement first, work reaches dev through pull requests and goes on to release and main, the checks are the ones the project runs, and the paused Sonar check is never taken as a pass.

Draw the marks of tool icons without a background the icon cannot resolve: a plus, a minus or a square on a badge filled from a theme variable showed as a solid dot, since an icon loaded as a picture does not see the page's variables.
Tint the document icon of Properties with the theme, as every other icon is.
Lay the quick backgrounds of the document out in equal columns across the panel, a little closer together, so No color ends where the other controls end instead of against the edge.
Give everything in Properties the side margins the other panels have; only its transform fields had them.
Let a page change keep up to the thousand layers a document may hold; it still refused more than a hundred and fifty.
Record the paint extension of the native format as a proposed decision, ADR-0033, awaiting owner review, with the scenarios of paints, SC-0107, and of the phone layout, SC-0108.

Keep the paint model, its validation, the blending of gradients and the colour models in the domain package, tested against geometric and colour oracles; a PDF rendered by MuPDF painted the same pixels as the canvas.

Record the owner's decisions on 0.6.0: ADR-0032, the brush carried by a path in the native format, is accepted, and the drawing tools are accepted visually for the maturity of this preview. The strict Sonar gate remains outstanding, so no scenario is marked Verified.

entries.summary: The Pen, the Pencil, the Paintbrush and path editing behave as a designer who knows Illustrator expects
breakingChanges: A path may carry a brush painted along it, which the Paintbrush draws. Migration: a document holding a brushed path is refused by earlier versions of this editor and of the API; keep a copy of the original, or take the brush off the paths in the path panel before opening the document there.

B selects the new vector Paintbrush instead of the raster brush, as it does in Illustrator. Migration: saved keyboard settings that still gave B to the raster brush as its old default hand it over automatically; to keep painting pixels with a key, assign one to the raster brush in Settings, Keyboard shortcuts.

changes.description: Draw with the Pen as in Illustrator: a click sets a corner and a drag a smooth anchor; Shift keeps a click on the angle increment; Space moves the anchor being placed; Alt during a drag splits the handles; a press on the first anchor closes the path and a drag there shapes the closing curve; a click on the last anchor takes its handle in and a drag pulls a new one; an endpoint of an open path continues it, the endpoint of another joins it, and Ctrl-click away from every object leaves the path open.
Show beside the cursor what a path tool would do: a new path, a continuation, a close, an added or deleted anchor, a conversion, a join or a freehand stroke.

Add and delete anchors with the Pen over a selected path, keeping the shape when an anchor goes; Shift, or a preference, keeps the Pen drawing. Alt turns the Pen into Convert Anchor, Add Anchor into Delete Anchor and back, the Scissors into Add Anchor and the Pencil into the Smooth tool.
Convert anchors as Illustrator does: a drag from an anchor pulls out two handles that move together, a click takes them in, and a drag on a handle breaks it away.

Choose segments with the Direct Selection tool and reshape a curve through the point grabbed, or move a straight segment whole; choose all the anchors of a filled path with a press inside it, and the anchors inside a marquee across objects, which then move together. Delete removes the chosen anchors and segments and leaves the rest as open paths.
Select groups outward with the Group Selection tool, beside Direct Selection and under Alt from it.
Fit the Pencil's strokes with Bezier curves by Fidelity and Smoothness, close them with Alt, extend or redraw a selected path started near, and join two selected paths with Ctrl.
Smooth the stretch of a path the Smooth tool is dragged along, and erase with the Path Eraser only what it passes over, keeping the rest curved.

Draw vector strokes with the Paintbrush, on B: a fitted path carrying a calligraphic brush of its own diameter, roundness and angle, painted the same on the canvas, in SVG and in PDF, which the path panel applies, changes and takes off.
Set the options of the Pencil, the Paintbrush, the Smooth tool and the Eraser by double-clicking the tool, with Illustrator's ranges and defaults, kept between sessions.
Join paths with Ctrl+J, asking for a corner or a smooth point when the ends meet, and Average anchors along either axis or both with Ctrl+Alt+J.
Simplify paths with a preview, curve precision, angle threshold, straight lines and the original shown behind, counting the anchors before and after.
Convert chosen anchors to corners or smooth points, remove them, and cut the path at them from the path panel; select stray points.
Stretch a path with the Reshape tool, beside Scale, from the focal points it is pressed on.
Erase vector artwork with a nib of its own shape, sized with [ and ], across every object when nothing is selected, on a straight line with Shift, or over a whole marquee drawn with Alt.

Turn a text into one shape per letter, each with the holes of that letter inside it, the letters of a word grouped together, the words grouped into the text and the whole thing kept inside the group the text belonged to. A selection of several texts outlines every one of them.

Import encapsulated PostScript drawings, the EPS files Illustrator and CorelDRAW export: their paths, colours and stroke widths arrive as editable layers, read with the names of the language and the aliases each program defines for them, and whatever falls outside that vocabulary is reported.

Show chosen anchors solid and the others hollow, handles only where Illustrator shows them, and the anchor under the pointer ringed, with anchor size, handle style, handles for several anchors and the highlight set in a Selection and anchor display category of Settings.

Carry a licence: the Ximply Design Studio Limited Use Licence, which lets anyone read the software and run it to evaluate it, to study it or for their own internal use, and keeps distribution, modification and commercial use for the author, who may grant them in writing.
Show the editor at work in the readme, above the address of the published preview, https://xds.ximplicity.es, and clone the default branch instead of a branch that was retired.

Publish the editor on the owner's preview address with `scripts/deploy-production.ps1`, which builds the checkout, uploads it under the commit it was built from, moves the link the web server reads and reloads it only after the configuration is accepted, keeping the earlier releases so a return to one of them is a single command.
Name the import command Import, not Import image: it reads drawings as well as pictures.
Show or hide the column of tools from View, Layout, like the other blocks of the workspace. The canvas takes the width the column leaves, and the choice is remembered.
Build the spatial preview by group, one plane per group, and offer a parallax view whose camera faces the planes and follows the pointer.

Show the same credits in the footer as the other product of the company: the copyright with the company and the author, the version that opens the about screen, and the links to LinkedIn, to Ximplicity and to the repository, each in its own tab.
Give the text tool a list of its own, so Create outlines sits beside the tool that writes the text; every tool family with a command of its own shows the arrow that opens its list.
Name what an outline of the stroke left alone in a selection of several objects, instead of doing nothing visible.
Run the keyboard commands of the editor while a text is being written or a field has the keyboard, committing what is written first, as Illustrator does; a field keeps the keys that write in it.
Create outlines and outline stroke did nothing from the Object menu, the list of the text tool or the context menu; every surface now reads one table of commands.
Keep the keyboard settings saved when a new command appears, instead of replacing every customised shortcut with the defaults.
Show and hide the Pivot and Selection blocks of the workspace from the Layout menu, whose entries did nothing.
Create outlines produced one shape for a whole text, in the colour of a new path, with open letter contours; each letter is now its own closed shape in the paint the text carried.
Keep the appearance popovers of the fill and the stroke on the screen.
Continuing a path from its endpoint no longer adds a second anchor on top of it.

Share one least-squares fitter among the Pencil, the Smooth tool and the Paintbrush, and keep path editing, erasing and joining in the domain package, where they are tested against geometric oracles rather than against their own output.
Record the brush carried by a path as a proposed decision, ADR-0032, awaiting owner review, since it extends the native format.

entries.summary: Drawings come in and go out as vectors, artwork is copied, repeated and outlined, and text becomes shapes
breakingChanges: A document may now hold up to a thousand layers instead of a hundred and fifty, which drawings imported from other tools often need. Migration: a file with more than a hundred and fifty layers is refused by earlier versions of this editor and of the API; keep the original file if you need to open it there.

The smallest side a layer may measure falls from one pixel to a hundredth of a pixel, so scaled drawings keep their shapes. Migration: a file holding such a layer is refused by earlier versions of this editor and of the API; keep the original file if you need to open it there.

changes.description: Import SVG drawings as editable native layers, with their shapes, paths, text, colours, stroke widths, transforms and groups, and report in the status line whatever the reader could not represent.

Duplicate in series with Ctrl+Shift+D: a linear series with its own step, turn and relative size per copy; a circular series around the pivot, with the copies turning with it or keeping their rotation; and a grid series with its columns, rows and gaps.

Copy, cut and paste artwork, with paste in front and paste in back, which keep the coordinates of the copy and place it immediately above or below the selected object. Copy is Ctrl+C, cut Ctrl+X, paste Ctrl+V, paste in front Ctrl+F and paste in back Ctrl+B.
Show or hide the bounding box of the selection, the frame with its handles and the rotation knob, with Ctrl+Shift+B.

Lay the list of documents in the export dialog out as a table with a heading, the document name on the left and its selection box on the right, alternating rows and a box that chooses or clears them all. The table is a component of its own, with multiple selection as a feature, so other lists can be built on it.
Offer the clipboard actions, the duplicate and the bounding box on the selected objects in the context menu, each with its key.

Add a copy and paste group to the tool rail beside the import action, with copy, cut, the three pastes, the duplicate and the duplication in series in its list of subtools, each enabled only when it applies.
Export as PDF, with the vector geometry of the drawing rather than a picture of it: paths keep their curves, strokes keep their dashes and text keeps its characters, drawn with the standard font.

Choose what to export from one dialog: the format, and which of the open documents are included, with the current one chosen to begin with. A PDF collects them as one page each; SVG and PNG write one file per document.
Print the chosen documents through the printing dialog of the browser, one page each, from the File menu or the export dialog.

Cut paths with two clicks: the scissors open a path at two of its own points, leaving independent open paths, and the knife divides the closed shapes its line crosses into two independent closed shapes. Both draw the cut in progress, both are undone in one step, and Escape forgets a cut that was started.

Edit the appearance of a whole selection from the properties: the fill, the stroke, its width, the line ends, the transparency and the blend mode reach every selected object, a group included, as one undo step. The place and the size stay with the object the form is showing.

Outline the stroke of any object from the Object menu or beside the tools that draw one: the line becomes the shape it painted, with the colour it had, and a shape that also carried a fill keeps it under its new band.

Turn text into shapes with Ctrl+Shift+O, the combination Illustrator uses, from the Object menu or beside the text tool: every letter becomes artwork with the fill, the place and the decoration the text had.

Carry three faces with the studio, each with the metrics of the family it stands for, so text is drawn the same on every machine and its outlines come from the very file that drew it. Families with no carried twin are outlined with the closest one, which the editor reports.
Give the line type of the stroke popover a block of its own, as wide as the popover, and keep the popover inside the screen by scrolling from where it opens instead of running past the bottom edge.

Switch between the preview and the outline view with Ctrl+Y or from the View menu: the outline view draws every layer as a hairline contour in one ink, without fills, colours, transparency or blend modes, with the frame of an image standing for it.
Scale proportionally while Shift is held during a corner drag, keeping the shape of the layer with its opposite corner fixed; the key used to snap the direction of the drag instead.

Close an imported path that carries a fill, which is what a drawing means by it: a shape left open in Illustrator arrives filled rather than empty, while a contour that is only stroked keeps its ends apart and one that is both filled and stroked arrives as the closed fill and the open stroke.

Import Illustrator and PDF drawings: the page of the file is read and its paths, colours and stroke widths arrive as editable layers, with the page turned upright and measured in pixels. Text, placed objects, inline images, gradients and clipping paths are reported instead of approximated.
Import ASCII DXF drawings: lines, polylines, circles, arcs, ellipses, points and text, with each drawing layer kept as a group and the drawing mirrored into document coordinates.

Fill an open path: a contour with a fill is painted as the drawing means it, on the canvas, in SVG and in PDF, while its stroke keeps its ends apart, which is how the drawing tools this studio follows behave.
Offer SVG and DXF beside the images in the import dialog, and refuse DWG, PDF and Illustrator files with the export that does work instead of a silent failure.

Repeat the last transformation with Ctrl+D: the move, the turn, the scaling or the duplication just applied is performed again on the selection, the copy it left behind included, and around the same pivot the original transformation used. A pivot placed by hand also travels to the copies a duplication makes, so successive repeats turn around one point.

Leave the original behind while transforming: holding Alt during a move, a turn or a scaling duplicates the objects on release. The original stays drawn in its place while the copy follows the pointer, the tool badge beside the cursor doubles and the cursor takes the copy sign, and the keys held at the moment of the release decide the outcome, so Alt can be pressed without moving the pointer again.
Raise the document size ceiling from 4096 to 8192 pixels, so A3 and A2 at 300 dots per inch can be set up and stored. A1 and A0 at that resolution stay out of range.
Prepare the raster layers of a PDF with an image element instead of a network request, which a strict content security policy can refuse.

Bring the transform pivot back with undo and forward with redo: each history step now carries the pivot it was taken with, and placing the pivot is a step of its own that leaves the artwork untouched.

Open a project whose drawing was scaled down: a layer may measure less than a pixel now, which a scaled drawing produces and the reader used to refuse, so files saved after scaling an imported drawing load again.

Read every imported file as data: no declared entity is expanded, no external reference is followed, nothing carried by a file is executed, and sizes, element counts and node counts are bounded before a layer exists. The font files the studio carries are served by the application itself and parsed in memory.
Let the document history carry the session state of each step beside the document, which is how the pivot travels with undo and redo.
Add a font reader and three carried faces, proposed in ADR-0031 and awaiting review, with their licences recorded in the notices shipped with the application.

entries.summary: Several documents in tabs, parametric construction tools, drafting dimensions, page setup, a movable transform pivot and brush controls
breakingChanges: Extended native-v2 paints and guide metadata require the updated reader. Migration: preserve original files and use this version for new saves; older readers may reject or discard these extensions.

changes.description: Work on several documents at once: New document and the tab strip plus button open a blank document in its own tab, and each tab keeps its content, undo history and selection. Tabs close one by one and show an unsaved-changes marker.
Add File > Clear to empty the active document, undoable, and ask in an in-app dialog before clearing or closing unsaved work.
Save projects with the .xds extension the documentation defines; files saved earlier as .ximply still open.

Draw connected wall runs where each click continues from the previous end with exact shared joints, choose whether a wall is centred on the drawn line or has a face on it, and end the run with Escape.
Give each door or window leaf its own mechanism, hinged, sliding, folding, pocket or fixed, choose how many leaves and the wall face they open towards, and add a passage without leaves.
Add a straight stair flight with a configurable width, length, number of steps and walking direction.
Set the line type of any stroke: solid, dashed, dotted, axis or a custom sequence of up to six dash and gap lengths.

Add chain dimensions, which measure consecutive spans against one offset line, and radius and diameter dimensions with their standard prefixes, one arrow on the arc or two through the centre and an optional centre mark.
Measure in metres, choose where the label sits along the dimension line, and unify the scale and label format of every dimension in the document with one switch.

Combine walls with the boolean operations and keep them parametric: collinear runs merge, a crossing wall splits the one it crosses, intersecting keeps the crossing piece and excluding keeps every arm. Ordinary artwork still combines into one plain object.

Set up the document from the transform tools: paper, screen and animation formats with output resolution and orientation, ruler units, margin guides with their centres, background colour, registration marks as a locked layer, and expanding or cropping the page.

Resize the page on the canvas by dragging handles on its corners and edges, with the rulers following live, or crop it by dragging the area to keep while the rest is dimmed. Escape cancels and one undo step restores the page.
Paint the page background like any other fill, with opacity, a colour picker and quick swatches for black, white, blueprint blue, chroma key green and no colour, which leaves the page transparent.

Add a transform pivot that scaling, rotation and mirroring work about. It starts at the geometric centre of the selection and is dragged by its own mark while unlocked, travels with the objects when they move, returns to the centre on a double press, and snaps to the centre, to the selection box, to artwork vertices and dimensions and to the active rulers, guides and grid. Its own controls lock it, show it and switch its magnetism.
Choose how the area selectors pick objects: every object the area touches, or only the ones it encloses.

Add brush subtools for the round, flat, calligraphy, marker, airbrush and pencil tips, with a control bar for the brush and the eraser: pressure, opacity, cadence, diffusion, a speed variation slider that runs from thinner to thicker around the nominal size, a blend mode and tip angle where they apply, and a sample stroke that previews the result.
Add a zoom area subtool: drag a rectangle and it fills the visible workspace on release; Ctrl with Space and a drag does the same with any tool active.
Add an Appearance section to the settings with the theme and how transparency is displayed, and choose how many decimal places measurements are shown with.

Apply drafting rules to linear dimensions: labels aligned with the line and never upside down, the line broken around the label when it fits, arrowheads moved outside and the label placed beyond the nearest end when the span is too small, a gap at the measured points, an overshoot past the extension lines and 3:1 arrowheads.

Pre-mark the snap point of the dimension tools with a small blue square on vertices, intersections, edge midpoints and points on edges, and preview the actual dimension while choosing its side and offset.
Snap new dimensions to the anchors and extension ends of existing ones and share their offset line when parallel, whenever dimension magnetism is on.

Snap wall drawing to existing wall ends and axes before the grid, and lean it to the nearest 45 degree direction within six degrees, which keeps plans orthogonal; a wall joint still wins over the tendency.

Draw door and window frames in the wall beside the clear opening, draw hinged leaves as panels with thickness towards the opening, and draw leaf travel as a broken projection line in the editor and in SVG exports.
Give new walls and pillars a construction appearance and draw openings as outlines instead of using the current drawing colours.

Name the pen tool Bézier, give its subtools and each brush tip an icon drawn in the same language as the control bar, and continue an existing unlocked open path when either of its ends is clicked, while a locked path still starts a new object.
Name each typography measure in the text properties by an icon and a tooltip rather than a written label, with icon and control on one line.
Lay out every panel header in the right column the same way, chevron and name together on the left and anything else pushed right, on a raised band closed off by a rule while the panel is open.
Show the guidance of the blend panel as one tip at a time, marked by a bulb, and only where the panel is blocked; nothing is shown while a blend can simply be made or edited.

Show an icon beside each boolean, align, transform, blend and grouping action, shorten the dimension and floor plan forms, group the opening leaves and the ruler tick switches under their own headings, and align each setting with its control.

Use one scrollbar appearance across the shell, give the context bar and the document tab strip the height their content needs, move the workspace choice to the header beside the language and show only the fill in the appearance block while the brush is active.
Open projects in the current tab when it is an untouched blank document, otherwise in a new tab, and remove the redundant quick Fill, Stroke and Width rows from the tool rail.
Keep each fixed dimension point after a click: the canvas treated the pointer capture released after every click as a cancellation, so the third click never created the dimension.
Draw walls as complete rectangles: composing their outlines dropped one corner, so a wall appeared as a triangle with its start edge collapsed.
Open the document dimensions dialog from its toolbar button, which did nothing because the command was only registered for keyboard shortcuts.
Open every dropdown on the theme colours: the property and header selects painted no background of their own, so under the dark theme the option list opened white with pale text.
Let the pivot mark take its own press wherever it rests; it used to hand the press to the object under it, which made the pivot unreachable at its default place.
Draw the two speed variation marks as round dots of a fixed size, centred with the slider; the larger one was stretched into an ellipse by the row.
Accept stair parameters in the floor plan property panel, and replace the native browser confirmation used by New document.
Generated documentation navigation is identical on Windows and POSIX hosts, with forward-slash links and case-sensitive document order.
Load the full editor stylesheet directly in production so the Content Security Policy does not leave the interface unstyled. Rebuild the local containers to apply the correction.

Use localhost:8090 by default for the local editor to avoid conflicts with port 8080. Existing installations should set XDS_PORT=8090 in .env.local and restart; credentials and saved projects are preserved.
Validate dash sequences, leaf mechanisms, opening sides, wall alignment, stair parameters, page setup and background paints in the native parser and in the authenticated API before storage.
Revalidate every restored local draft with the native document parser and bound local recovery to 12 tabs of 4 MB each.
Share one dimension geometry between Canvas, SVG export, hit testing and the placement preview, and derive projection curves instead of storing them.
Keep boolean results on walls parametric by clipping their axes rather than their outlines.
Keep every new parameter optional so existing documents open unchanged, and store local recovery per tab, migrating the earlier single-document draft automatically.

The contribution check accepts GitHub merge button commits when GitHub verified the signature, the author is the owner and the pull request title used as message is a Conventional Commit; the web merges of PR #16, PR #17 and PR #18 join the pinned historical exemptions.
Add the GitHub web merges of PR #13 and PR #15 on dev to the pinned legacy-commit exemptions by exact SHA and reason, without rewriting history.
Temporarily pause the Sonar quality job at the owner's request, preserving its commented analysis steps and strict policy for reactivation; skipped analysis is not passing quality evidence.
Add a disposable SonarQube trial with pinned images, real coverage inputs, retained findings and automatic container/volume teardown. This diagnostic run does not replace the strict integration gate.
Exercise the actual trial image-resolution and teardown commands with regression tests, including preservation of unrelated containers. These tests do not claim a live scan.
Record incremental product checkpoints and explicit branch/version feedback as permanent project instructions.
Retry temporary connection resets while the disposable server starts; sanitize transport errors before writing diagnostic output.
Add native-v2 absent/alpha paints and nonprinting guide metadata with matching API validation, renderer tests and measurement preferences; interface integration is in progress.
Retain only dev, release, main and active work branches; close pending PRs and remove retired branches without promoting unverified code.
Validate proposed commit and PR wording before publication and identify failing commit revisions in contribution diagnostics; retain all existing policy restrictions.
Record the PR integration preflight and distinguish passing build checks from the required product quality gate.
The contribution check accepts two pinned historical GitHub merge commits on dev by exact SHA and reason, without rewriting history; all other commits remain fully checked.

entries.summary: Connected wall runs, leaf mechanisms with opening side, stairs, chain dimensions and dashed line types

changes.description: Draw connected wall runs: each click continues the wall from the previous end, and the segments share exact joints. Escape ends the run.
Choose whether a wall is centred on the drawn line or has its left or right face on it.
Give each door or window leaf its own mechanism: hinged, sliding, folding, pocket or fixed, and choose the wall face the leaves open towards.
Add a passage without leaves for open doorways.
Set the line type of any stroke: solid, dashed, dotted, axis or a custom sequence of up to six dash and gap lengths.
Add a straight stair flight with a configurable width, length, number of steps and walking direction.
Add a chain dimension tool that measures consecutive spans against a single offset line in one step.
Add radius and diameter dimensions with their standard prefixes, one arrow on the arc or two through the centre, and an optional centre mark.

Add a transform pivot: scaling, rotation and mirroring work about it, it starts at the geometric centre of the selection and is dragged by pressing on its own mark, which always takes that press while the pivot is unlocked. A press anywhere outside the mark moves the selected objects and carries the pivot with them, and a locked pivot hands every press to the artwork. Its own controls in the top bar lock it, show it and switch its magnetism, which attracts it to the geometric centre, to vertices and edges, to dimensions and to the active rulers, guides and grid.
Measure in metres, choose where the label sits along the dimension line, and unify the scale and label format of every dimension in the document with one switch.

Combine walls with the boolean operations and keep them as walls: collinear runs merge, a crossing wall splits the one it crosses, intersecting keeps the crossing piece and excluding keeps every arm, all as parametric walls. Ordinary artwork still combines into one plain object.
Add a zoom area subtool: drag a rectangle and it fills the visible workspace on release; Ctrl with Space and a drag does the same with any tool active.

Add brush subtools for the round, flat, calligraphy, marker, airbrush and pencil tips, and a control bar for the brush and the eraser with pressure, opacity, cadence, diffusion and a speed variation slider that runs from thinner to thicker around the nominal size, plus a blend mode and tip angle where they apply and a sample stroke that previews the result, swelling and thinning as the speed slider dictates.

Resize the page on the canvas by dragging handles on its corners and edges, with the rulers following live, or crop it by dragging the area to keep while the rest is dimmed. Escape cancels and one undo step restores the page.

Set up the document from the transform tools: paper, screen and animation formats with output resolution and orientation, ruler units, margin guides with their centres, background colour, registration marks as a locked layer, and expanding or cropping the page.
Choose how many decimal places measurements are shown with.
Choose how the area selectors pick objects: every object the area touches, or only the ones it encloses.
Paint the page background like any other fill: opacity, a colour picker and quick swatches for black, white, blueprint blue, chroma key green and no colour, which leaves the page transparent.
Add an Appearance section to the settings with the theme and how transparency is displayed: checkerboard on or off and the size of its squares.
Draw the plan section of the frame at each side of a door or window.

Name the pen tool Bézier and give its subtools matching icons: the same pen with a plus, a minus or a square badge, and give each brush tip an icon drawn as the stroke it paints, the same language the control bar uses.
Carry on drawing an existing Bézier path: clicking either end of an unlocked open path with the pen continues it instead of starting another object, while a locked path still starts a new one.
Save projects with the .xds extension, the native extension the documentation defines; files saved earlier as .ximply still open.
Draw leaf travel as a broken projection line in the editor and in SVG exports, scaled with the stroke width.
Draw door and window frames in the wall beside the clear opening instead of inside it, and draw hinged leaves as panels with thickness towards the opening.
Snap wall drawing to existing wall ends and axes before the grid, so corners and T junctions meet exactly.
Lean wall drawing to the nearest 45 degree direction when the angle is within six degrees of it, which keeps plans orthogonal; a wall joint still wins over the tendency.
Give new walls and pillars a construction appearance and draw openings as outlines instead of using the current drawing colors.
Snap new dimensions to the anchors and extension ends of existing ones, and share their offset line when parallel, whenever dimension magnetism is on.
Shorten the dimension label form and group its settings under their own heading.
Show an icon beside each boolean, align, transform, blend and grouping action, and narrow the tool option list.
Give the dimension lock the same styled toggle as the guide lock, and explain the local preview badge, which now opens the local service settings.
Use one scrollbar appearance across the shell, and give the context bar and the document tab strip the height their content needs so neither scrolls vertically.
Group both ruler tick switches under a single Snap to ruler ticks label in the unit settings.
Move the workspace choice to the header beside the language, and show only the fill in the appearance block while the brush is active.

Drag the pivot by its mark with the selection tool as well, wherever the mark rests: it used to give the press to the object under it, which made the pivot unreachable at its default place. The dragged position snaps to the centre of the selection, to the corners, side middles and sides of the selection box, and to the vertices of other artwork within the snapping distance.

Name each typography measure in the text properties with an icon and a tooltip instead of a written label, with the icon and its control on one line: size, weight, leading, letter, word and paragraph spacing, baseline shift and both scales.

Carry a pivot placed by hand with the selection it belongs to: moving the objects by dragging or with the arrow keys keeps the pivot at the same place within them, and a cancelled drag returns it. Rotating, scaling and mirroring still leave the pivot itself in place, since they turn around it. Unlocking the pivot is therefore what allows moving it independently.
Send the pivot back to the geometric centre of the selection by double clicking its mark, while the pivot is unlocked.

Show the guidance of the blend panel as a tip, marked by a bulb, and only where the panel is blocked: when a member is locked, when the step count has reached its limit, when fewer than two objects are selected and when the selected pair does not qualify. One tip at a time, and none at all while the blend can simply be made or edited. The note on editing endpoints is dropped; both endpoint buttons already explain themselves.

Lay out every panel header in the right column the same way: the chevron and the name together on the left and whatever the header carries on its right edge pushed there, all on one vertically centred line. Drawing tools and Blend objects pushed their name to the right edge. Each header now sits on a raised band closed off by a rule while the panel is open, so where one panel ends and the next begins is visible, and the chevron is an icon that turns with the open state.
Draw the two speed variation marks as round concentric dots of a fixed size, centred with the slider; the larger one was stretched into an ellipse by the row.
Open the document dimensions dialog from its toolbar button: the command was only registered for keyboard shortcuts, so the button did nothing.

Open every dropdown on the theme colours: the option list of the property and header selects took the browser colours because those controls painted no background of their own, so under the dark theme it opened white with pale text.
Draw walls as complete rectangles: composing their outlines dropped one corner, so a wall appeared as a triangle with its start edge collapsed.
Validate dash sequences, leaf mechanisms, opening sides, wall alignment and stair parameters in the native parser and in the authenticated API before storage.
Derive projection curves instead of storing them, and share one geometry between Canvas, SVG and hit testing.
Keep every new parameter optional so existing documents open unchanged.

entries.summary: Multiple documents in tabs, File > Clear with unsaved-change protection and professional linear dimensions

changes.description: Open several documents at once: New document and the tab strip plus button open a blank document in a new tab, and each tab keeps its own content, undo history and selection.
Add File > Clear to empty the active document; it is undoable.
Ask for confirmation in an in-app dialog before clearing or closing a document with unsaved changes.
Close tabs individually; tabs show an unsaved-changes marker.
Pre-mark the snap point of dimension tools with a small blue square on vertices, intersections, edge midpoints and points on edges.
Preview the actual dimension while choosing its side and offset.
Align linear dimension labels with the dimension line, never upside down, and break the line around the label when it fits.
Move arrowheads outside and place the label beyond the nearest end when the space between extension lines is too small.
Keep a gap between measured points and extension lines, overshoot the dimension line and draw 3:1 drafting arrowheads.
Open projects in the current tab when it is an untouched blank document, otherwise in a new tab.
Remove the redundant quick Fill, Stroke and Width rows from the tool rail; the overlapping fill and stroke squares keep the full appearance picker.
Keep each fixed dimension point after a click: the canvas no longer treats the pointer capture released after every click as a cancellation, so the third click creates the dimension.
Replace the native browser confirmation used by New document.
Revalidate every restored local draft with the native document parser and bound local recovery to 12 tabs of 4 MB each.
Store local recovery per tab and migrate the earlier single-document draft automatically.
Share one dimension geometry between Canvas, SVG export, hit testing and the placement preview.

entries.summary: Editable parametric walls, doors, windows and pillars
breakingChanges: New native-v2 procedural parameters and wall-host references require compatible readers. Migration: preserve original files and use this version or newer for new saves; SVG/PNG retain visible geometry but not editable parameters or host relationships.

changes.description: Add procedural wall, door, window and pillar tools with editable parameters and generated vector geometry.
Configure door/window leaf widths and supported swing or sliding representations; choose rectangular or circular pillars.
Host openings on walls so their cutouts and placement follow the host.
Join compatible crossing walls and shared end faces while preserving source objects, group membership and ordinary artwork stack boundaries.
Close shared wall corners with miter joins, retaining flat free endpoints and bounded bevel fallbacks at acute angles.
Recompute supported procedural contours from native parameters for Canvas rendering and SVG export; cut openings only from their host and retain physical wall thickness under shear.
Reject procedural elements and dimensions in native blend definitions before derived blend geometry can overwrite them.
Use a bounded local registry of trusted geometry functions; native files store declarative parameters, never executable code.
Validate parameter shapes and host references in both the application and API.
Keep this preview scoped to two-dimensional vector plans, without BIM, structural validation, building-code certification or external CAD-format fidelity.

entries.summary: Vector dimension annotations, line endpoints, contextual grouping and ruler subdivisions
breakingChanges: New native-v2 dimension, line-end and regroup metadata requires compatible readers. Migration: preserve original files and use this version or newer for new saves; SVG/PNG exports preserve visible annotations but not editable dimension semantics or regroup history.

changes.description: Add linear and angular dimension tools with singular-point placement assistance, editable measurement formatting and a movable label handle.
Configure dimension scale, display units, decimal count and separator per annotation, carrying formatting defaults to subsequent dimensions.
Add independent start/end markers: arrow, open arrow, triangle, dot, slash, cross or none, with size, tip/base placement and linked editing.
Add Group, Ungroup and Regroup to contextual menus according to selection membership; retain edits and nested parent groups when restoring prior membership.
Add numeric displacement and rotation entry for selected objects, groups and Bezier anchors with an explicit rotation center.
Add dimension visibility, lock and snapping controls beside the existing measurement aids.
Preserve annotation glyph and marker shapes during object transforms; customize dimension lines, extension lines and label typography.
Configure major/minor ruler intervals and their snapping independently, while retaining the global ruler magnet and screen-space tolerance.
Preserve multiple selection when opening its context menu and leave independent objects unchanged when ungrouping selected groups.
Validate dimension, endpoint and regroup extensions in native documents and API contracts; share annotation geometry between Canvas and SVG.
Keep dimensions as independent captured annotations rather than persistent CAD constraints. Radius/diameter, tolerances and chain/baseline dimensions remain outside this preview.
Migrate missing minor ruler preferences from the existing major interval without changing native artwork coordinates.

entries.summary: Area selection tools with remembered mode and Shift toggling

changes.description: Add rectangular, circular and freehand lasso subtools to Selection, with localized icons/tooltips and live area previews.
Reuse the last area-selection mode when dragging empty canvas with the normal Selection tool; persist the last mode locally.
Hold Shift during area selection to toggle reached objects against the starting selection, adding unselected objects and removing selected ones.
Preserve ordinary object movement and transforms, respect groups and locked/hidden layers, and exclude editing guides.
Cancel area selection with Escape or pointer cancellation without changing artwork or document undo history.
Use bounded geometric area intersection and document-coordinate previews without changing native documents or API contracts.

entries.summary: Blue ruler markers follow the canvas cursor

changes.description: Show a blue cursor projection on each visible ruler: a vertical mark at X on the horizontal ruler and a horizontal mark at Y on the vertical ruler.
Keep markers aligned through zoom and scrolling, independently of the full-canvas cursor-axes setting. Hide them when the cursor leaves the canvas or an editing dialog is active.
Reuse viewport-aware cursor coordinates and noninteractive overlays without changing document or preference formats.

entries.summary: Editable vector blends with intermediate steps, easing and expansion
breakingChanges: Optional native-v2 blend definitions require an updated reader. Migration: preserve original documents before saving live blends; older readers may reject the new metadata. Expand blends before exchanging editable objects without the live relation.

changes.description: Blend two compatible vector objects or equally sized vector groups from back to front, interpolating vertices, handles, geometry, colors, alpha, stroke width and opacity.
Edit intermediate step count and linear, ease-in, ease-out or ease-in-out distribution.
Edit retained endpoints and regenerate intermediate objects; expand to independently editable objects or release to retain only the original endpoints.
Expose localized blend actions and endpoint editing controls; expanded objects support ordinary grouping and ungrouping.
Preserve undo and native save/load, and export materialized intermediate artwork through existing SVG/PNG rendering.
Validate blend metadata and reference ownership in frontend/API, with bounded subdivision, layer count and group depth.
Support compatible vector contour topology and equal-cardinality groups. Text/image blends, editable spines and path-following orientation remain outside this preview.

entries.summary: Stroke alignment, joins, caps and scoped eyedropper/bucket tools
breakingChanges: Optional native-v2 strokeStyle metadata requires an updated reader. Migration: preserve original documents before saving new stroke properties; older readers may reject new metadata. Absent metadata retains the legacy centered round stroke.

changes.description: Configure center, inside or outside stroke alignment on closed vector contours through the shared stroke picker.
Choose round, bevel or miter joins and butt, projecting square or round caps using localized icon controls.
Sample semantic object styles with Eyedropper and apply current styles with Paint Bucket, choosing fill, stroke or both. Stroke transfer includes alpha, width, alignment, joins and caps.
Preserve existing shortcut assignments when introducing style tools; conflicting new default bindings remain unassigned.
Record style application in undo history and preserve new stroke defaults when drawing subsequent objects.
Keep stroke geometry consistent between canvas and SVG, including compound closed contours and independent paint alpha.
Validate stroke metadata in frontend/API native-v2 readers and symbol definitions.

Open contours and live text use centered stroke alignment. Style sampling reads object properties, not image pixels; bucket applies object styles rather than region flood filling or live-paint topology.

entries.summary: Settings category navigation with one active form panel

changes.description: Navigate settings through a left-hand category menu and edit only the selected category in the right-hand panel.
Preserve all existing settings and their values, with localized category navigation, keyboard access and responsive layout.
Keep long forms separately scrollable and cancel unfinished shortcut recording when changing categories.
Record the owner's settings layout requirement in repository instructions and UX guidance for future categories.
Record undo-memory limits, clearing history, temporary directory and default work directory as future requirements, without exposing unimplemented controls.

entries.summary: Editable typography and text frame sizing with shared canvas and SVG composition
breakingChanges: Optional native-v2 typography and text-layout metadata may be rejected by older readers. Migration: preserve original documents and use the updated application for new saves; legacy text without metadata retains its rendering behavior.

changes.description: Select font family, weight and style; configure leading, letter, word and paragraph spacing, horizontal and vertical scale, baseline offset, alignment and decoration.
Text property toggles control wrapping, automatic English/Spanish hyphenation, content sizing, horizontal or vertical automatic sizing and shrink-to-fit within a fixed frame.
Text layout uses shared canvas/SVG glyph positions and browser font measurements. Automatic frame changes and multi-object property updates are undoable.
Add a persistent global guide-lock button immediately before Guides, reusing the layer padlock icons. Existing guides cannot be dragged while locked; rulers still create new guides.
Replace compact action labels with icons and localized tooltips while preserving form labels, accessible names and menu shortcuts.
Display text dimensions and spacing in configured units while retaining canonical pixel values.
Preserve fixed text frame dimensions during text editing; automatic sizing is explicit.
Add strict matching frontend/API text metadata validation and bounded layout calculations.
Pin the hyphen dependency to 1.14.1 for automatic English/Spanish hyphenation; retain its distributed license notice.

Fonts depend on system availability. Inline editing uses a native textarea: its caret and selection may differ from composed artwork for justification, automatic hyphenation or scaling. This release does not implement per-character styles, linked frames, text on paths or complete OpenType controls.

entries.summary: Target-aware menus for objects, groups, guides and Bezier nodes

changes.description: Right-click canvas objects, groups, guide lines or layer rows for grouped visibility, deletion and stacking actions. Move one step or to either end within the containing group; groups move as complete units.
Right-click selected Bezier anchors or handles to convert corner/smooth nodes, collapse or expand either handle independently, or delete the vertex.
Show current configured shortcuts when the contextual action matches a registered command; support keyboard navigation and outside dismissal.
Preserve native context menus in text fields. Locked targets disable destructive actions; stale targets are rejected after document edits.
Display explicit units beside additional dimensional properties. The canvas cursor remains hidden while its axis guides are visible, independently of the optional tool badge.
Keep guide context menus accessible when guides are locked without permitting locked dragging.
Context targets capture document revision, exact layer/group scope and node indices. Actions are undoable and do not modify unrelated siblings.

entries.summary: Shared alpha paint picker, configurable units and editable magnetic guides
breakingChanges: Native-v2 now supports absent/alpha paints and guide metadata that older readers may reject or discard. Migration: preserve original files and use this version for new saves; reverting the application does not convert new files. Guides are intentionally omitted from PNG and SVG exports.

changes.description: Open the same fill/stroke picker from Appearance, the inspector or overlapping swatches below the two-column toolbar. Choose a color, no color, black or white and edit independent color opacity and stroke width.
Swap fill and stroke without losing their transparency. Paint alpha remains separate from overall layer opacity.
Configure distance and font units independently using px, pt, mm, cm, inches or feet. Rulers and dimensional controls convert their display and input without resizing artwork.
Show or hide rulers, guides and grid with paired magnetic buttons. Configure ruler step, grid spacing and each source's magnetic radius in Settings.
Drag horizontal or vertical guides from rulers, reposition them and drag them outside the artboard to delete them. Guides persist as ordered layers with visibility, locking and undo support.
Reorder layers by dragging, preserving grouped artwork together.
Toggle Appearance, Workspace and Measurement context blocks through View > Layout; visibility preferences persist.
Move theme switching beside the language selector in the header, using sun/moon icons for the current theme.
Match snapping distance to screen pixels across canvas zoom and preserve the pointer offset while moving objects.
Keep guide layers out of artwork rendering, exports, 3D preview and normal artwork operations.
Preserve independent fill/stroke alpha through native files, authenticated API storage, Canvas and SVG.
Validate paint strings, guide metadata, finite coordinates and bounded measurement preferences without weakening storage authentication.
Use 96 document pixels per inch and 72 points per inch; these units do not assert physical monitor calibration.
Keep ruler generation bounded and canonical document geometry in pixels. Full quality certification remains separate from feature-branch preview publication.

entries.summary: Edit Bezier points with Selection and constrain handle drags

changes.description: Edit anchors and direction handles on a selected curve using Selection as well as Direct Selection.
Hold Shift while dragging anchors, handles or new Pen tangents to constrain their direction to the angle increment in Settings, relative to the canvas axes.
Hold Ctrl or Alt while dragging a handle to move it independently without moving the opposite handle. Unmodified smooth handles remain coupled.
Preserve curve controls and the active gesture when Ctrl changes during a drag; temporary Ctrl selection remains available while idle.
Preserve selected anchors when Shift starts a constrained drag; a Shift-click can still deselect an anchor.
Clear stale node selections when changing layers and ignore direction handles hidden by Settings.
Apply path edits with the effective selection tool instead of accidentally invoking the underlying drawing or anchor-deletion tool.
Add geometry and routing regression checks, including transformed paths, modifier changes, undo and cancellation. Native files and API contracts remain compatible.

entries.summary: Follow the canvas cursor with optional horizontal and vertical guides

changes.description: Show horizontal and vertical guides across the canvas, intersecting at the pointer, with a crosshair cursor.
Enable or disable cursor axes with a Settings toggle; the choice persists between sessions and is independent of the tool-icon setting.
Keep guides aligned through canvas zoom and scrolling, clipped to the canvas, and hidden outside it or while editing text.
Extend existing local input preferences with an optional boolean; existing settings default to enabled and native documents remain compatible.

entries.summary: Organize drawing controls in a grouped two-column toolbar

changes.description: Arrange toolbar buttons in two columns, grouped by selection, drawing, paint, transformation and navigation, followed by appearance controls.
Expose Selection and Direct Selection side by side while preserving tool flyouts, configured shortcuts and tooltips.
Place related operations together and adjust the workspace width and flyout placement for the wider rail.
Preserve native document and API compatibility; no data migration is required.

entries.summary: Identify the local preview and dismiss menus on window blur

changes.description: Run the local launcher with info to identify the source version, branch and commit without starting Docker or reading credentials.
Print the source version, branch and commit after successfully starting the local preview. About and the footer show the new preview version.
Close main menus and tool flyouts when leaving the browser window; preserve expandable inspector panels and reset temporary input state.
Add regression checks for window-blur dismissal and checkout identification, including operation without Git.
Preview publication does not certify the strict integration gate; existing quality and browser-acceptance limitations remain.

entries.summary: Editable cubic paths, drawing tools and configurable input
breakingChanges: New saves use native document format 2 for curves, subpaths and symbol metadata. Earlier readers cannot open these files. Format 1 import remains supported.
Tool defaults change to M Rectangle, L Ellipse, P Pen, N Pencil, Shift+E Eraser and R Rotate. Configurable shortcuts replace the temporary preview bindings.

Migration: Preserve original .ximply files before opening and saving them with this version. Review Settings and resolve shortcut collisions before saving preferences. Keep the new application for v2 files: reverting the application does not downgrade documents. Existing server artifacts follow the same reader-version boundary. Rebuild local containers; retain .env.local and project volumes.

changes.description: Draw editable cubic paths with Pen and edit anchors/handles with direct selection, anchor addition/deletion and corner/smooth conversion.
Construct lines, rounded rectangles, polygons, stars, arcs, spirals, rectangular and polar grids and flares alongside existing shape tools.
Refine paths with smooth, simplify, average, join/close, scissors, path eraser, filled-vector eraser and stray-point cleanup.
Trace images in monochrome, grayscale or color using bounded editable scanline output; retain source images and update, expand or release a trace.

Create linked symbols; redefine, replace and expand instances; import/export local libraries; spray and manipulate instances with shift, scrunch, size, spin, stain, screen and initial style operations.

Select multiple objects; create and dissolve nested groups; align in six directions and distribute horizontally or vertically. Combine vectors with union, subtract, intersect or exclude; raster and text are excluded from boolean operations.

Expose Rotate, Reflect and Scale tool families through triangular flyouts, with sibling choices dismissed by outside interaction or Escape. Reflect preserves editable flip flags for vectors, images and text; numeric transforms also support selected groups.
Configure shortcuts with collision detection, Shift constraint angle and the optional lower-right cursor tool badge in Settings.
Replace the starter example with an editable branded cover, including a cubic X mark and grouped vector studies.
Hold Ctrl for temporary Selection; release it to restore the drawing tool without losing unfinished Pen paths.
Add explicit canvas zoom buttons.
Add visible rotation and four edge handles; edge scaling affects only its local dimension. Shift constrains rotation and linear transformations to the chosen angle.
Edit existing text inline using the Text tool.
Show active shortcuts in menus and tooltips; close custom dropdowns and menus when interacting elsewhere. Ctrl+Space+wheel zooms the canvas while preserving UI scale.
Keep About reachable from Help and the footer; company links open in a new tab.
Prevent accidental text selection in interface labels while preserving selection in inputs, text areas and editable content.
Load the full production stylesheet directly without a CSP-blocked inline handler.
Use localhost:8090 by default. Existing installations should update XDS_PORT in .env.local; saved projects and credentials are retained.
Generate identical documentation links and ordering on Windows and POSIX hosts.
Continue validating native versions and bounded geometry; imported documents and symbol libraries do not execute code. Existing bearer storage boundaries remain.
Collect whole-source frontend, API and engineering coverage; enforce fresh Sonar evidence in a separate fail-closed CI check. Coverage and unavailable analyses still block integration.
Keep drawing geometry separate from Angular; carry native format changes through renderer, SVG and API validation.
Pin polygon-clipping 0.15.7 for filled-vector erasure. Curves are sampled at 24 steps per segment, so erased geometry is approximate.
Tracing is limited to 64 pixels per side; contour fitting remains pending.
Preserve rotated child geometry during nonuniform group transforms using optional native-v2 skewX; keep curve controls and symbol-instance state during transformations.
Nine-slice resizing uses a fixed 25 percent inset. Editable registration and slice guides and a full graphic-style library remain pending.
Record the mandatory integration preflight and preview feedback cadence.
Preserve exact historical commit exemptions and the unchanged quality policy. Current build/test/CI evidence is recorded in the implementation handoff, not inferred from earlier releases.

entries.summary: Validated local container preview

changes.description: Validate all four resize handles and preserve the opposite anchor for rotated layers.
Honor the configured version-file path in containers without assuming the repository directory depth.
Render zero-width vector strokes consistently in the canvas and SVG export.
Verify packaged frontend delivery, bearer-token rejection, artifact save/open and the About deep link in disposable Docker services.
Record the local trial commands and preserve the strict pre-merge quality requirements.

entries.summary: First local drawing and image-retouching preview

changes.description: Draw editable rectangles, ellipses, freehand vector paths and text.
Select, move, resize and rotate layers; control visibility, locking, opacity, order and blending.
Import PNG, JPEG and WebP images; paint and erase raster pixels with undo and redo.
Adjust image brightness, contrast, saturation and blur without discarding the source image.
Save and reopen editable .ximply files; export flattened PNG or SVG with embedded raster layers.
Inspect separated document planes in a Three.js spatial view with orbit, pan and zoom.
View bundled Markdown release notes in About and select versions with a shareable version URL.
Add a responsive workspace, collapsible and reorderable side panels, centralized themes and English/Spanish interface labels.
Keep small drafts in browser storage and provide explicit project-file downloads for larger documents.
Resolve the API authentication dependency and preserve source-version identity in API health and OpenAPI metadata.
Preserve transparent backgrounds when rendering separate spatial layers.
Protect server artifact save/open with a bearer token configured locally and kept out of the frontend bundle.
Bind the Docker preview to loopback, validate native documents and restrict artifact identifiers to generated UUIDs.
Limit project size, layer counts and local artifact storage; reject remote image URLs in native project data.
Pin Angular 22.1.7 and its compatible build/test toolchain; record package lockfiles and container image digests.
Add domain, renderer pixel, editor-state and API tests plus local Bash/PowerShell launchers.

This preview does not implement production Keycloak integration, PostgreSQL/TypeORM transactions, collaboration, desktop windows, third-party plugin installation or full Illustrator/Photoshop format compatibility.

entries.summary: Navigable documentation and quality evidence

changes.description: Organize the documentation into linked feature, scenario, decision and product-outcome indexes.
Add scoped context lookup and validation of document metadata, links and reachability.
Use the authoritative navigable methodology instead of the frozen draft as the project reference.
Add a revision-bound SonarQube evidence collector with stale-analysis and concurrent-update rejection. Live server validation remains pending.
Include engineering harness code in the required quality module inventory.
Provide versioned Markdown release notes and generated assets for the future application About screen.

entries.summary: Initial design foundation

changes.description: Document the proposed architecture, product scope, contracts, security, licensing and delivery controls.
